meta.notes: Source for the Library/Antilibrary pages, the home Library tile (homepage: true) and the MCP get_books tool. Covers come from Open Library via scripts/fetch-covers.mjs and are stored in public/images/covers (self-hosted). Books with noCover use a generated cover. Shelves on the Library page appear in the order of meta.shelves. scripts/check-books.mjs runs before every build and blocks duplicates, unknown shelves and missing covers. Library books marked mustRead: true show a Must read label.

library.title: The Daily Stoic
library.author: Ryan Holiday & Stephen Hanselman
library.why: Good daily habit and grounding. Focus on what you can control. I find it a more manageable format than sitting down and reading something like Meditations.

library.title: Principles: Life and Work
library.author: Ray Dalio
library.why: Principles by Dalio is a must-read. Process of your decision-making and radical transparency have been a game changer.

library.title: The Challenger Sale
library.author: Matthew Dixon & Brent Adamson
library.why: A selling approach that's fit me very well: being able to provide valuable insight that's tailored to each stakeholder, controlling the buying conversation through those uncomfortable discussions.

library.title: 12 Rules for Life
library.author: Jordan B. Peterson
library.why: If you're considering reading it or life feels chaotic, it's probably a must-read for you.

library.title: Beyond Order
library.author: Jordan B. Peterson
library.why: A good balance to his first 12 rules: the next steps once your house is in order.

library.title: The One Year Uncommon Life Daily Challenge
library.author: Tony Dungy & Nathan Whitaker
library.why: Character, honor, family, friendships.

library.title: Wisdom for Each Day
library.author: Billy Graham
library.why: Another daily book; a good alternative to Dungy or The Daily Stoic if you're looking for this.

library.title: Think Again
library.author: Adam Grant
library.why: Treat your beliefs as hypotheses. Seek evidence that could change your mind. Taking a more scientifically grounded perspective on what you think you know.

library.title: Can't Hurt Me
library.author: David Goggins
library.why: If you need a motivator, get the audiobook and start running.

library.title: Building a Second Brain
library.author: Tiago Forte
library.why: Might be an unpopular opinion, but with all the AI tools anymore, this book is a little dated at this point.

library.title: Meditations
library.author: Marcus Aurelius
library.why: Must read at some point. That we have the insights we do from such a great and thoughtful leader.

library.title: Integrity Selling for the 21st Century
library.author: Ron Willingham
library.why: Understand your customer and create real value. Kind of adjacent to Challenger selling.

library.title: Little Red Book of Selling
library.author: Jeffrey Gitomer
library.why: Understand why people buy.

library.title: Rhinoceros Success
library.author: Scott Alexander
library.why: Always keep moving forward. It's a fun read that brings the energy.

library.title: Leadership and the One Minute Manager
library.author: Ken Blanchard, Patricia Zigarmi & Drea Zigarmi
library.why: Develop people's ability and confidence rather than keeping them dependent on supervision. Worth a read once you're managing people.

library.title: The Ten-Day MBA
library.author: Steven Silbiger
library.why: It might take you more than 10 days, but it's a good base.

library.title: The 10% Entrepreneur
library.author: Patrick J. McGinnis
library.why: Don't quit your job before you start your company. Worth an answer, considering that.

library.title: Helping Surgeons Treat Their Patients Better
library.author: Arthrex (company history)
library.why: The Arthrex Way: How the Arthrex Juggernaut was built and continues to lead on innovation.

library.title: Never Split the Difference
library.author: Chris Voss & Tahl Raz
library.why: Great book for understanding negotiation.

library.title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
library.author: Dale Carnegie
library.why: A little dated, but still holds true. Listen, show interest and appreciation, and respect.

library.title: The Intelligent Entrepreneur
library.author: Bill Murphy Jr.
library.why: Entrepreneurship is not just a personality trait but a learnable discipline. Walks you through a bunch of different experiences.

library.title: Broken Money
library.author: Lyn Alden
library.why: Understanding money as a technology. Likely the best Bitcoin book I've read, but gets there from first principles and not in your face about it. Fascinating read.

library.title: The Hidden Cost of Money
library.author: Seb Bunney
library.why: Interesting how the properties of the money you use can influence personal behaviors.

library.title: Capital Wars
library.author: Michael J. Howell
library.why: Probably need to reread this two or three times to fully understand. I'm only on my first pass through. Fascinating take on global liquidity, cross-border flows, banking credits, financing, and how those cycles drive markets.

library.title: The Most Important Thing
library.author: Howard Marks
library.why: Good assets don't necessarily mean good investments. A way to apply second-level thinking and patience for investors.

library.title: The Dao of Capital
library.author: Mark Spitznagel
library.why: Austrian. Sometimes the patient and roundabout way is the best way to achieve the long-term objectives. Really changed how I thought about portfolio allocations.

library.title: The Big Print
library.author: Lawrence Lepard
library.why: The inflation chapter is probably the best chapter of a book I could recommend to anyone on inflation.

library.title: Bitcoin Age
library.author: Nik Bhatia
library.why: Pair this with Layered Money, Banking History, and Rise of the Dollar. It's a fun read on not the most exciting topics.

library.title: Security Analysis: 100 Page Summary
library.author: Preston Pysh & Stig Brodersen
library.why: Condensed guide for security analysis; they do a great job of explaining concisely.

library.title: The Price of Tomorrow
library.author: Jeff Booth
library.why: Technology should make many goods and services cheaper, which is in direct tension with how our economic system is set up. A thought-provoking book. Once you read it, you always find yourself looking at things through its lens.

library.title: The Psychology of Money
library.author: Morgan Housel
library.why: Your behaviors can matter more than your technical sophistication when it comes to money. Worth a read.

library.title: The Creature from Jekyll Island
library.author: G. Edward Griffin
library.why: Long but entertaining read. Interesting if you're wondering how we got here.

library.title: The Bitcoin Standard
library.author: Saifedean Ammous
library.why: Must-read book if you want to understand and invest in Bitcoin.

library.title: Layered Money
library.author: Nik Bhatia
library.why: Money is not uniform. There are layers: base assets. He does a good job of explaining the hierarchy of these assets.

library.title: The Fourth Turning
library.author: William Strauss & Neil Howe
library.why: Generational experiences affect the other generations. Some of it seems common sense, but they put a framework to it.

library.title: The Sovereign Individual
library.author: James Dale Davidson & William Rees-Mogg
library.why: Predictions have been pretty accurate; worth the read on that alone. Develop portable skills.

antilibrary.title: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
antilibrary.author: Joseph Campbell

antilibrary.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
antilibrary.author: Ben Horowitz
